timeRange.note: Marsh & Rowe (2020) give the age as Sinemurian-Pliensbachian (Kayenta Formation); the Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 stage boundaries. Two PBDB records of cf. Dilophosaurus are dated Hettangian-Sinemurian.

massKg.note: Single published estimate (NHM Dino Directory); method not stated.

text.en: Dilophosaurus was a meat-eating dinosaur about 7 metres long that lived in what is now Arizona in the Early Jurassic, roughly 200 to 184 million years ago. It is named for the pair of crests on top of its head, which probably helped it recognise its own kind or attract a mate, and were likely too weak for fighting. It was the largest land animal known from North America at that time.
Its fossils were first thought to be a new species of Megalosaurus. Only after a skull with crests was found did it get its own name in 1970.
It was the largest animal known to have lived on land in North America during the Early Jurassic.
